messages.subject: vertical UI layout?
parts:
I have a complex app with two order of tabs:
- Higher tabs to navigate the app according to a specific workflow with different types of data manipulation.
- Lower tab where the user can select different graphical / reporting options.

Currently the problem I am experiencing is that the lower part appears at different points on the screen, depending on the number of items in the higher part.

Ideally I would need to be able to divide my screen in "rows", with the ability to tell where a certain element can start (similar to bootstrap where I have 12 columns and the "column" keyword in shiny).

What could I do to make sure that the lower part always start at the same row?

Example code:

library(shiny)

a <- "Test"
##
runApp(list( ui = fluidPage(
  navbarPage(a, id = "main",
# tabPanel("Overview", id="overview"), 
tabPanel( "Supply-Demand", id="spdm" ,
 tabsetPanel(
         tabPanel("Overview" ), 
         tabPanel("Demand"      ),
        tabPanel("Activity"   ),
        tabPanel("Resources"  ),  
        tabPanel("Assign"  )  
        ), # end of tabset panel
       tabPanel("reporting", br(),
       tabsetPanel(
         tabPanel("graph"),
         tabPanel("Pivot Table")
        )  )
 ) , 
tabPanel("Administration", id="admin")
)), 
 server = function(input, output, session) {

}))
########

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: vertical UI layout?
parts:
You would have to fix the size of the top element I suppose, you can do that with CSS, give your tabsetPanel an ID and then do:

tags$style(type="text/css",
  "#tabsetpanelid { height: 600px; overflow: auto }"
)

where tabsetpanelid would be the ID of your tabsetpanel.
